forecasts.question: Will Iran publicly commit to resuming mediated ceasefire negotiations (a named Iranian official or MFA announces readiness for talks) before EOD 2026-09-06?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-AMBIGUOUS (→ NO per ambiguity rule). Horizon 2026-09-06 passed 23 days ago. Iranian President Pezeshkian stated circa September 1 that Iran 'would return to the ceasefire agreement if the US does' (Fortune, Sep 1). This is an explicitly conditional offer. F2's ambiguity rule: 'conditional or preconditioned offers = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO unless the US publicly accepted the condition.' The US did not accept: Trump's September 9 statement ('talks possible, war to end after election') and the five-tanker-destruction operation the same day confirm no acceptance before EOD Sep 6. No unconditional public commitment by a named Iranian official was found in the record before the Sep 6 horizon. Functional resolution: NO.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-09-06, a named Iranian official (FM Araghchi, Supreme National Security Council, or IRNA/Tasnim/Press TV quoting an official) issues a public statement committing to resuming or entering mediated ceasefire negotiations with the United States. A 'readiness for talks' declaration counts; mere written-message relay does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: One TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera) citing the named Iranian official, OR Iranian state media (IRNA/Tasnim) carrying the official statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Conditional or preconditioned offers ('will talk if US stops strikes') = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO unless the US publicly accepts the condition; a mediator asserting Iran is 'open' without a named Iranian official statement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO (per written criteria; resolution-criteria discrepancy flagged for human review). The Knesset dissolved July 17, 2026 at mandatory natural term end — the first completed parliamentary term since 1988 (Al Jazeera, Times of Israel 2026-07-17). Coalition vote: 62-0 (coalition held 61+ seats through dissolution; never dropped below 61-seat majority). Election date: exactly October 27 — neither 'earlier than' Oct 27 nor 'loss of majority' before Oct 27. Strict criteria yield NO on both tests. Discrepancy note: the question's spirit — did the Netanyahu government lose its governing mandate before Oct 27? — points to YES given the July 17 dissolution ended the coalition's operational role. But the written criteria require explicit majority loss or an earlier election, neither of which occurred. RESOLVED-NO per written criteria. HUMAN_REVIEW: F7 resolution-criteria discrepancy noted; future regime-change forecasts should model 'natural term dissolution' as an explicit pathway.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

forecasts.question: Will the US issue a formal substantive response to Iran's September 24 UNGA ceasefire road map (via named official, Qatari mediators, or public statement) before EOD 2026-10-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: New 72h forecast. Iran delivered a written 60-day ceasefire road map to Witkoff/Kushner on September 23-24, with SNSC Secretary Rezaei attaching a '4-5 day' deadline (expiring approximately Sep 28-29). Trump publicly rejected the '7-day Hormuz plan' on September 26; Waltz called it 'a pretty cynical attempt.' Araghchi responded September 27 that Waltz 'has not read' the proposal; Iran described it as covering a ceasefire, Hormuz reopening, and a structured talks timeline — broader than the Hormuz-only piece Trump rejected. As of September 29, Araghchi met Qatari mediators; sources (India TV/ANI) report the US reply is expected 'hopefully today' (Sep 29) or Monday. Shuttle diplomacy is operationally active. p=0.45: a formal response within 72h is expected given the pace, but Trump/Waltz's framing and the stated deadline already being past modestly discount the probability.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-10-02, a named US official (Witkoff, Kushner, Waltz, Trump, or Secretary of State) issues a formal response — via Qatari mediator readout, US government statement, or press briefing — that addresses Iran's September 24 60-day ceasefire road map with specific terms, conditions, or a counter-proposal. A rejection with specific stated conditions for US re-engagement also counts as a qualifying formal response.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: One TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera) citing the named US official, OR an official Qatar/Pakistan government mediator readout attributed to US position.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump's September 26 rejection of the '7-day Hormuz plan' alone does NOT qualify unless a TIER1 source explicitly frames it as a formal US response to the full September 24 60-day road map. Generic 'talks are proceeding' statements without named US position on the road map = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A mediator message not publicly attributed to a named US official = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US hold a formally convened indirect session (both delegations physically present in same venue, named mediator on-site, named principals from both sides) between 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-13?
forecasts.delta_reason: New 14-day forecast. The September 22-23 UNGA session (Araghchi/Witkoff/Kushner, Qatar PM Al Thani on-site, ~3 hours) established that both sides can physically convene with a named mediator. Oman's Foreign Ministry announced a date for the next round of talks. However, as of September 28-29, the format has reverted to shuttle diplomacy (Qatar running messages between separately-located delegations). A jump back to a convened session requires a positive US response to the Sep 24 road map. Trump's NBC comment ('always thinking about resuming strikes') and political calculus ('war to end after election') are bearish. Araghchi faced domestic backlash from hardliner factions over the September 22-23 session (IranWire Sep 24), constraining his latitude. p=0.38 reflects the established precedent of convening, the Oman announcement (bullish), offset by shuttle-only posture since Sep 23 and the domestic IRGC pressure on Araghchi (bearish).
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports that both US and Iranian delegations (named principals at senior official/envoy level) attended a formally convened negotiating session at the same venue, with a named mediator (Oman/Qatar/Pakistan/Switzerland) on-site, between 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-13.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1, OR one TIER1 plus an official mediator government readout naming both US and Iranian delegations present.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Shuttle diplomacy in which Qatar or Oman runs messages between separately-located US and Iranian delegations = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Phone or video-mediated calls = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. The distinction from the September 22-23 UNGA format is that both delegations must be physically co-located in the same venue.

forecasts.delta_reason: New 42-day forecast. Israeli President Herzog designates the party leader with the best coalition-forming path. Most September polls give Eisenkot's bloc ~54 seats vs Netanyahu's ~50; the i24NEWS outlier reverses this. Small-party arithmetic at the 3.25% threshold can swing 4-6 seats between blocs. Likud recovered from an August low of 19 to ~20-21 ('gaining ground') but remains behind Yashar in four of five polls. Base rate for an incumbent caretaker-PM coalition achieving mandate in a wartime election with net-negative approval: ~30-35%. p=0.35 reflects the competitive but Netanyahu-disadvantaged polling with 28 days of remaining campaign volatility. Resolution horizon is 14 days post-election (by November 10) for the mandate step.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Israeli President Isaac Herzog publicly designates Benjamin Netanyahu as the person tasked ('mevakesh lehakil') to attempt to form a coalition government, within 14 days after official preliminary election results are published following the October 27, 2026 election.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: One TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Times of Israel/Haaretz) citing President Herzog's official announcement.
